title: Pinched simplices give a weakly equivalent mapping resolution
statement:
Use simplicial categories [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and right mapping spaces [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Define $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ to have objects $0,\ldots,m$ and, for $i\leq j$, mapping set the ordinary nerve of the inclusion poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing $i,j$, with empty mapping set for $i>j$ and union as composition. Monotone maps act by images of subsets. Put $\mathfrak C[S]=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^m\to S}\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ in simplicial categories. Put $J^n=(\Delta^n\star\{y\})\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}$, where the join is $\Delta^{n+1}$ with last vertex $y$ and the whole initial face $\Delta^n$ is collapsed to $x$. Set $Q^n=\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)$; monotone maps of initial faces make $Q$ a cosimplicial simplicial set. For $K$ a simplicial set define $|K|_Q=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}K_n\times Q^n$, the quotient of the coproduct of copies of $Q^n$ by the simplicial and cosimplicial identifications. Define $(\operatorname{Sing}_QT)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(Q^n,T)$. These functors are adjoint by evaluation. There is a natural cosimplicial map $p:Q\to\Delta^\bullet$ inducing a weak homotopy equivalence $p_K:|K|_Q\to K$ for every simplicial set $K$. For every Kan complex $T$, the evaluation counit $e_T:|\operatorname{Sing}_QT|_Q\to T$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

For a quasicategory $S$ and vertices $x,y$, there is a natural weak homotopy equivalence
$$\theta_{S,x,y}:|\operatorname{Map}^{R}_S(x,y)|_Q\longrightarrow\mathfrak C[S](x,y).$$
Here an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}^{R}_S(x,y)$ is a map $J^n\to S$ sending the displayed vertices to $x,y$. On the corresponding copy of $Q^n$ the map $\theta$ is the mapping-set map induced by $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathfrak C[S]$. All these maps commute with simplicial operators and maps of the displayed inputs; $Q^0=\Delta^0$ and the maps in degree zero take the displayed vertex to itself.

source.place: Section 2.2.2: the cosimplicial object Q, Proposition 2.2.2.7 and Corollary 2.2.2.10; Section 2.2.4, Proposition 2.2.4.1. No Stacks tag states the pinched mapping resolution.

proof.text: The subset-poset formulas give simplicial enriched categories: union is associative and has singleton endpoint identities, and direct image commutes with union. Simplicial categories have the required colimits by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Extending the formulas over simplex colimits therefore defines $\mathfrak C$, and applying it to the maps of pinched simplices defines the cosimplicial $Q$. A map $|K|_Q\to T$ is exactly a family $K_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(Q^n,T)$ compatible with every monotone map; the quotient identifications are exactly the equations for a simplicial map $K\to\operatorname{Sing}_QT$. This gives the natural adjunction, with counit evaluation on each copy of $Q^n$. The same description shows that $V(K)=|K|_Q$ preserves all small colimits: compatible maps from either iterated colimit into an arbitrary $T$ are the same families.

Apply [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. In its quotient model the maximum map on nonempty subsets is unchanged by erasing the coordinates below a coordinate constantly equal to $1$, so it descends to $p^n:Q^n\to\Delta^n$. Direct image along a monotone map $f$ satisfies $\max f(I)=f(\max I)$; hence the $p^n$ form a cosimplicial map. The same node gives weak contractibility of $Q^n$, the equality $Q^0=\Delta^0$, and injectivity of every latching map. By the coend relations, $V(\Delta^n)=Q^n$ and $V(\partial\Delta^n)=L_nQ$: a map from either side is precisely a compatible family on all proper faces. Thus every image boundary inclusion is a monomorphism.

source.place: Section 2.2.2, cubical description, Remark 2.2.2.6 and map preceding Proposition 2.2.2.7

proof.text: Every collapse $Q^n\to Q^0$ is a weak equivalence because its source and target are weakly contractible. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] to the colimit-preserving $V$ and the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], using the boundary and collapse facts just established. It follows that $V$ sends monomorphisms to cofibrations, preserves all weak homotopy equivalences, and $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ is a Quillen adjunction.

The cosimplicial map induces a natural map $p_K:V(K)\to K$, identifying $|K|_{\Delta^\bullet}$ with $K$ by $[\sigma,\alpha]\mapsto\sigma\alpha$. Prove it is a weak equivalence first for finite simplicial sets, by induction on dimension and then on the number of top-dimensional nondegenerate simplices. Here finite means finitely many nondegenerate simplices. The empty case is the identity on the empty simplicial set. In dimension zero, $K$ is a finite coproduct of points and $V(K)$ is the same coproduct since $Q^0=\Delta^0$, so $p_K$ is an isomorphism. For dimension $n>0$, removing a top-dimensional simplex lowers its number, and its boundary has dimension at most $n-1$, so the two induction parameters strictly decrease where used. For a simplex, $p_{\Delta^n}:Q^n\to\Delta^n$ is a weak equivalence since both spaces are contractible. Remove one top-dimensional nondegenerate simplex to write $K=K'\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n}\Delta^n$. The two spans for this pushout and its image under $V$ have boundary-to-simplex monomorphisms, and the three comparison maps are weak equivalences by the induction and simplex case. The gluing assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] proves the induction step. Every simplicial set is the filtered union of its finite simplicial subsets: a simplex generates a finite subset because its finitely many nondegenerate faces generate it, and finite unions stay finite; uniqueness of the nondegenerate representative is [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. Since $V$ preserves colimits, the filtered-colimit assertion of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] proves the claim for arbitrary $K$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, full skeletal and filtered-colimit induction

proof.text: All simplicial sets are cofibrant in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Thus $V$ itself computes its left derived functor on the ordinary homotopy category. The natural weak equivalence $p_K$ makes this derived functor naturally isomorphic to the identity, hence an equivalence. For a Kan complex $T$, the object $T$ is fibrant and $\operatorname{Sing}_QT$ is cofibrant. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] to the Quillen adjunction of step 3: its ordinary counit $e_T$ is a weak equivalence. By the adjunction bijection of step 1 this is the specified evaluation map, rather than an unspecified weak equivalence between the two objects.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.9 and Corollary 2.2.2.10; Hovey Lemma 1.3.10 and Proposition 1.3.13

proof.text: Let $E=S_{/y}$, whose $n$-simplices are maps $\Delta^n\star\{y\}\to S$ restricting to $y$ at the cone vertex. Its projection $a:E\to S$ is a right fibration, and $E_x=\operatorname{Map}^R_S(x,y)$, by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Use the cone definition of $\operatorname{St}$ in [lem-coef-right-straightening-fiber-comparison]. Over a point this is $V$: both preserve colimits, and on $\Delta^n$ the cone pushout is exactly $J^n$ and its mapping set $Q^n$. For every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the map between these pushouts restricts to $\Delta(\alpha)$ on the initial face and fixes the new cone vertex; it therefore induces exactly $Q(\alpha)$. The identifications on simplices consequently respect every coend relation, giving the natural identification on all simplicial sets. Consequently the fiber-comparison assertion supplies a weak equivalence $f':V(E_x)\to\operatorname{St}_S(E)(x)$. There is a simplicial evaluation map $E\star\Delta^0\to S$ sending the new cone vertex to $y$: on a simplex of $E$ append its already specified terminal vertex $y$. It agrees with $a$ on $E$. Applying $\mathfrak C$ and the pushout defining $\operatorname{St}$ gives $f'':\operatorname{St}_S(E)(x)\to\mathfrak C[S](x,y)$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.3.15 and Proposition 2.2.4.1, factorization through the straightening of S/y

proof.text: Write $e=\operatorname{id}_y\in E$. There is an explicit contraction $H:E\times\Delta^1\to E$ from the identity to the constant $e$, fixing $e$. For an $n$-simplex $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to S$ of $E$ and a monotone $t:[n]\to[1]$, send index $j\leq n$ to $j$ if $t(j)=0$ and to $n+1$ if $t(j)=1$, and send the extra terminal index to $n+1$; precompose $\sigma$ with this monotone map. To check operators, write $h_{n,t}$ for this index map. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ and its terminal-vertex extension $\alpha^+$, one has $\alpha^+h_{m,t\alpha}=h_{n,t}\alpha^+$: at $j\leq m$ both sides equal $\alpha(j)$ when $t(\alpha(j))=0$ and equal $n+1$ otherwise, and both take the extra index to $n+1$. Thus the formula defines a simplicial map; at $t=0$ it is the identity, at $t=1$ it is the constant simplex $e$, and it fixes $e$. Put $A=(E\times\{1\})\cup(\{e\}\times\Delta^1)$. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow E\times\Delta^1$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to $\{1\}=\Lambda^1_1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $\{e\}\hookrightarrow E$. The arrow $\{e\}\hookrightarrow E$ is its retract: its section has domain $e\mapsto(e,0)$ and codomain $z\mapsto(z,0)$; its retraction is constant to $e$ on $A$ and $H$ on $E\times\Delta^1$. The two composites are identities and $H|_A=e$. Thus $\{e\}\hookrightarrow E$ is right anodyne by the retract closure in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. This statement is about underlying simplicial sets; to view the retraction over $S$ give the cylinder the map $aH$ to $S$. In particular the actual inclusion over $S$, $e$ mapping to $y$, satisfies the hypothesis of the straightening theorem.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.4.1, retract of the right-anodyne cylinder inclusion; Corollary 2.1.2.7

proof.text: By [lem-coef-right-straightening-fiber-comparison], the map $g:\operatorname{St}_S(\{e\})(x)\to\operatorname{St}_S(E)(x)$ is a weak equivalence, and adjoining the single arrow $y\to v$ identifies its source canonically with $\mathfrak C[S](x,y)$. Under this identification the composite $f''g$ is the identity: the evaluation map takes the adjoined arrow to $\operatorname{id}_y$, so every arrow into $y$ is unchanged. Two-out-of-three makes $f''$, and then $f''f'$, weak equivalences. For an $n$-simplex $\tau:J^n\to S$ of $E_x$, the cone pushout defining the restriction of $f''f'$ is the pushout collapsing the initial $\Delta^n$ to $x$. Thus on its copy of $Q^n$ this composite is exactly $\mathfrak C[\tau](x,y)$, proving that it is the specified $\theta$. Coend identifications give compatibility with every simplicial operator; functoriality of simplex colimits, cone evaluation and pushouts gives compatibility with every map of $(S,x,y)$. Finally $J^0=\Delta^1$ and $Q^0=\Delta^0$; a vertex represented by an edge $x\to y$ is sent to that same edge in $\mathfrak C[S](x,y)$. The maps $p$ and evaluation in degree zero likewise send their displayed vertex to its value. This covers $x=y$, identity edges, and empty mapping spaces without choosing a filler or a path.

split_report.summary: Eight steps construct the coend adjunction and maximum map, prove p by skeletal induction and filtered colimits, identify the evaluation counit through the ordinary derived adjunction, and factor theta through straightening the right slice. The right-anodyne retract and the identification of the actual canonical composite are written explicitly. Four smaller statement-only inputs remain; the coherent-nerve theorem is not cited because it depends on this item. Statement unchanged. Second reading defines the join cone inline, makes the finite induction and simplex-operator checks explicit, and limits the auxiliary filtered-colimit statement to the source's filtered-poset scope.

This realizes the pinched resolution subargument of lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison without changing the chapter or unit route.

HTT and Hovey are not in literature/ and network access is blocked here, so I could not open them at the cited pages. Instead I checked each step against HTT 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.9, 2.2.3.15 and 2.2.4.1 and Hovey 1.3.13 and 5.2.6 from my own knowledge, and recomputed the small cases by hand. Steps 1–8 hold. In step 2, max is constant on the identified classes and V(boundary)=L_nQ. In step 3, the hypotheses of boundary-collapse-test are met. In step 4, the induction has its base cases, the EZ (Eilenberg–Zilber) pushout holds and the finite subcomplexes form a nonempty filtered poset.
